fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. The LORD says, “…even the sound of a windblown leaf will put them to flight.” (Leviticus 26:36) Not a trumpet and not an army, just a leaf. I think this one is heavy.

A king? Friend, you went shopping in the wrong verse! The first thing the LORD names is “…rains in their season…” (Leviticus 26:4) After that come the land's produce and the trees' fruit. No throne in sight, just weather and fruit trees.

Gold! Baker, I like how you think. But gold has never watered a single field. The LORD starts with “…rains in their season…” (Leviticus 26:4) Then the land yields its produce and the trees bear their fruit.

Fifty is a big number, friend, but it's not the one in the verse. The LORD says, “Five of you will pursue a hundred…” (Leviticus 26:8) That's five Israelites chasing a hundred enemies. Then it jumps to ten thousand, and I need to sit down.

Wet grain? Nobody in this verse is complaining about soggy grain, friend! The LORD says, “You will still be eating the old supply of grain when you need to clear it out to make room for the new.” (Leviticus 26:10) The trouble here is a storeroom that's too full. I'd take that trouble any day.

Small isn't the word, baker. The verse says, “You will still be eating the old supply of grain when you need to clear it out to make room for the new.” (Leviticus 26:10) The old grain is still being eaten while the new grain arrives. Nothing in the verse calls the supply small.

That's right, baker. The LORD says He is the one “…who brought you out of the land of Egypt so that you would no longer be slaves to the Egyptians.” (Leviticus 26:13) He points back to what He already did for them. He adds that He broke the bars of their yoke.

It's the other way around, friend. The LORD says the wild animals will “…destroy your livestock…” (Leviticus 26:22) Livestock is on the list, along with their children and their numbers. It's a hard verse.

True, baker. The LORD says, “…you will eat but not be satisfied.” (Leviticus 26:26) Ten women bake the bread in a single oven, and it's doled out by weight. They do eat, and it still isn't enough. I think this one is heavy.

The verse says the opposite, friend. The LORD says, “…I will refuse to smell the pleasing aroma of your sacrifices.” (Leviticus 26:31) That comes right after He says He'll reduce their cities to rubble and lay waste their sanctuaries.

False is right, baker. The LORD says, “I will reduce your cities to rubble and lay waste your sanctuaries, and I will refuse to smell the pleasing aroma of your sacrifices.” (Leviticus 26:31) So the answer is the refusal, not the aroma.

Yes, baker. The LORD says, “…the land shall enjoy its Sabbaths all the days it lies desolate…” (Leviticus 26:34) The land gets its Sabbaths while the people are in the land of their enemies. Verse 35 says it will have the rest it did not receive during the Sabbaths when they lived in it.

Yes, baker. The verse says these are the laws the LORD established “…between Himself and the Israelites through Moses on Mount Sinai.” (Leviticus 26:46) Moses is the one the LORD sent to bring His people out of Egypt (Exodus 3:10). That's the closing line of the whole sermon.

Zion isn't named in this passage, friend. The verse says the LORD established these laws “…through Moses on Mount Sinai.” (Leviticus 26:46) Moses is the one the LORD sent to bring His people out of Egypt (Exodus 3:10). Sinai is the mountain.

Carmel doesn't show up here, baker. The closing verse says the LORD established these laws “…through Moses on Mount Sinai.” (Leviticus 26:46) Moses is the one the LORD sent to bring His people out of Egypt (Exodus 3:10). Sinai is the mountain named.
